title: The Lion King
synopsis: Pride Rock. Your father is king. Your uncle has a plan. The savanna stretches forever, until it doesn't.

nodes.text: Sun, savanna, Rafiki lifting you above. Elephant Graveyard comes either way; its meaning changes with the difference between “Stay close to Mufasa” and “Wander early.” At Elephant Graveyard, the decision will matter as memory as well as intent.

choices.consequence: You stay close to Mufasa. The path to Elephant Graveyard opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.
You commit to wander early. It carries you toward Elephant Graveyard, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: Scar tells you about it. You and Nala explore. Both choices lead to Hyenas, but “Go anyway” arrives there with a different cost than “Stay near home.” At Hyenas, the decision will matter as memory as well as intent.

choices.consequence: You commit to go anyway. It carries you toward Hyenas, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.
You commit to stay near home. It carries you toward Hyenas, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: They corner you. Mufasa arrives. You cannot avoid Father's Lesson; you can only decide whether “Run” or “Stand” defines the person who reaches it. By Father's Lesson, the people waiting will remember which instinct carried you forward.

choices.consequence: You choose to run. By Father's Lesson, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.
You choose to stand. By Father's Lesson, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

nodes.text: Stars and ancestors. The kings of the past watch. Both choices lead to Stampede, but “Believe” arrives there with a different cost than “Doubt.” At Stampede, the decision will matter as memory as well as intent.

choices.consequence: You commit to believe. It carries you toward Stampede, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: Scar's plan. Wildebeests in the gorge. Both choices lead to Mufasa Saves, but “Climb the tree” arrives there with a different cost than “Run with them.” In Stampede, the rules change the moment you decide they can be tested.

choices.consequence: You choose to climb the tree. By Mufasa Saves, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

choices.consequence: You see it. The path to Run opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: Scar tells you to run. You believe him. Hakuna Matata is already waiting. What changes is whether “Run far” or “Run nearby” is the instinct you carry into it. By Hakuna Matata, the people waiting will remember which instinct carried you forward.

nodes.text: Remember who you are. Run Home comes either way; its meaning changes with the difference between “Vow” and “Doubt.” By Run Home, the people waiting will remember which instinct carried you forward. Rafiki watches to see whether memory becomes courage.

choices.consequence: You choose to vow. By Run Home, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

nodes.text: Pride Rock is a wasteland. Hyenas everywhere. Sarabi will follow either decision, but it will meet a different version of you after “Climb quietly” than after “Roar.” At Sarabi, the decision will matter as memory as well as intent.

choices.consequence: You climb quietly. The path to Sarabi opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: Your mother sees you. Briefly, she sees Mufasa. The road still runs toward Scar's Confession. Its next turn depends on the difference between choosing “Embrace her” and choosing “Stand back.” At Scar's Confession, the decision will matter as memory as well as intent.

choices.consequence: You choose to embrace her. By Scar's Confession, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

nodes.text: They turn on Scar. The rock is yours. Rain will follow either decision, but it will meet a different version of you after “Rain comes” than after “Mourn the dead.” By Rain, the people waiting will remember which instinct carried you forward.

choices.consequence: You commit to rain comes. It carries you toward Rain, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: Rain on the rock. Sun after. Both choices lead to Cub, but “Roar” arrives there with a different cost than “Stand quiet.” At Cub, the decision will matter as memory as well as intent. The rain cannot choose what kind of king steps into the sunlight.

choices.consequence: You choose to roar. By Cub, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.
You choose to stand quiet. By Cub, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

nodes.text: Years later. Rafiki lifts your child. Kings of the Past comes either way; its meaning changes with the difference between “Hold Nala's hand” and “Stand alone.” In Cub, the rules change the moment you decide they can be tested.

choices.consequence: You choose to hold Nala's hand. By Kings of the Past, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.
You commit to stand alone. It carries you toward Kings of the Past, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: You teach your child the stars. The cycle is, again, a circle. “Pass it on” draws you toward King; “Keep it private” leaves The Council waiting on the other side. A third choice, “Take the third path,” keeps Circle in play.

choices.consequence: You choose to pass it on. By King, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.
You choose to keep it private. By The Council, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.
Some endings reveal themselves last. You choose to take the third path. By Circle, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

nodes.text: You rule for decades. The savanna heals. Songs are sung about you. Some of them, sweetly, are about Pumbaa. The road into King began with “Pass it on” in Kings of the Past; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.

You build a council with hyenas at the table. The pride disagrees. The pride is, in the end, stronger for it. The road into The Council began with “Keep it private” in Kings of the Past; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.

You die old. Your cub becomes the next ruler. They, in turn, raise their own. The circle, you decide, is exactly as small as it ever was. And exactly as wide. The road into Circle began with “Take the third path” in Kings of the Past; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.
